summary: Emma Georgina Rothschild is a historian who studied at Somerville College (1964–1967) and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (1967–1968). She later held professorships at the University of Cambridge around 1999 and Harvard University around 2008.

Emmie te Nijenhuis is an Indologist who studied at Utrecht Conservatory, Utrecht School of the Arts, and Utrecht University, completing her PhD under Jan Gonda (~1964–1970). She taught Indian musicology at Utrecht University (1964–1988) and served at the University of Amsterdam.

Enamul Haque was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned degrees from the University of Dhaka and the University of Oxford. He led the Bangladesh National Museum (1962–1991) and the International Centre for Study of Bengal Art (1995–2022).

Encho Tamura was a Buddhist studies scholar and historian. Educated at Kyushu and Kyoto universities, he held long-term academic appointments at Kumamoto University (~1954–1982) and Kyushu University (1941–1980), later directing the Kyushu Historical Museum and Fukuoka Human Rights Center.

Endō Asai was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saga High School, the University of Tokyo, and Rissho University. He held academic posts at Minobusan University, Nihon Fukushi University, Rissho University Junior College, and Rissho University, ultimately serving as president of Minobusan University.
Eng Jin Ooi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Mahidol University by 2021. The doctorate was supervised by Giuliano Giustarini, Peter Skilling, and Kengo Harimoto.

Enga Teramoto was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Kumbum Monastery in 1903. He later served as a lecturer at Kyoto University (~1908–1916) and as a professor at Otani University in 1915.

Enichi Ocho was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at the University of Tokyo under Daijo Tokiwa. He worked as a researcher at the Academy of Oriental Culture in 1931 and served at Otani University (1949–1976).

Enryo Inoue was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa and Tanzan Hara. He founded the Philosophical Society of Japan and Toyo University, where he taught from 1887 to 1905.

Ensho Kanakura was an Indologist and philosopher of Buddhism who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tohoku University (1926–1960) and Rissho University (1957–1974), and served as president of Miyagi University of Education in 1967.
Ensho Kobayashi is a scholar in Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Hanazono University, attested in 1988, and later as professor emeritus, attested in 2026.
Ensho Nasu is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Ryukoku University under the supervision of Esho Mikogami, attested in 1996.

Enshu Kurumiya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the Australian National University in 1974. He served as a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University, attested between 1981 and 1985.

Erberto Lo Bue was a scholar of Tibetology and history who earned his PhD from SOAS University of London (~1976–1981). He lectured in Tibetan language and literature at the University of Milan (~1995–2002) and later taught at the University of Bologna (~2002–2016).

Eric David Mortensen is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his PhD from Harvard University (attested 2003) under the supervision of Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, Michael Witzel, and Kimberley C. Patton.

Eric Haruki Swanson is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He has held academic posts at Loyola Marymount University and served as a Senior Visiting Scholar at Stanford University, attested in 2026.
Eric Huntington is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago, where he studied under the supervision of Gary A. Tubb.

Eric J. Sharpe was a religious studies scholar and Indologist who studied at the University of Manchester and Uppsala University. He held the First Chair of Religious Studies at the University of Sydney (1977–1996) and a professorship at Uppsala University (1978–1981).

Eric M. Greene is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley under Robert H. Sharf. He holds a post in religious studies at Yale University, attested from 2017 to 2026.

Eric Stephen Goodell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed master's degrees at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and the University of Virginia, where he studied under the supervision of Paul Groner (attested 2012).
